title: Graded SLI handbook for short-lived traffic bias and circuit breaker heuristics
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Several production incidents during short-lived traffic spikes showed that flat-window SLIs over-5m obscure burst behavior and force coarse-grained load-shedding that impacts high-priority routes. Goal: produce a compact, implementation-ready handbook that defines graded SLIs (multi-window, burst-weighted), error-budget consumption semantics for per-endpoint and per-model-variant contracts, and a matched set of circuit-breaker heuristics and failover gating thresholds for multi-region routing. The handbook must be prescriptive enough for engineers to implement SLI calculation, for SRE to tune circuit hysteresis, and for product owners to declare degradation tiers for customer-facing routes.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SLI schema (fields + units + sampling cadence) that supports at least three windows: instantaneous (30s), short (5m), and medium (1h)
Definition of burst-weighted error budget consumption that accounts for tail latency and short-lived error spikes (formula and example calculations)
Circuit-breaker state machine with concrete thresholds (trip, half-open probe, backoff multiplier) and region-aware overrides documented
A validated mapping from SLI grades to load-shedding actions (soft degrade, variant fallback, regional failover) with per-tier customer-visible outcomes
End-to-end test plan and telemetry queries for on-call to verify correct SLI calculation and circuit behavior in staging
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created after post-incident review (INC-2025-02-09) recommended burst-aware SLI work
2025-02-18: Spike session with runtime and routing owners; agreed to canonicalize 30s/5m/1h windows and add token-weighted latency component
2025-02-22: Draft formula for burst-weighted burn rate reviewed; concern raised about noise for low-volume routes — proposal to add minimum-volume floor
2025-02-26: Prototype SLI aggregator implemented in metrics-pipeline branch; initial synthetic tests show expected higher sensitivity to 30s spikes
2025-03-01: Design review scheduled with SRE and Console teams to align UI surface for graded-SLI visualization
decisions: Adopt triple-window SLI (30s/5m/1h) with exponential decay weighting toward recent samples
Error budget burn will be token-weighted for gen routes (tokens_out + tokens_in * 0.1) to reflect cost and work per request
Circuit breakers will be regional and per-model-variant; global routing will prefer healthy regions but allow prioritized soft-fallbacks
Low-volume routes (below 1 req/min) will use a higher smoothing window and a minimum-event floor to avoid flapping
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Burst-sensitive SLIs could create false positives for low-traffic endpoints. Mitigation: implement minimum-volume floor and smoothing for low-volume routes.
Risk: Token-weighted burn favors short responses, may bias scheduling. Mitigation: calibrate weight (0.1) in staging with cost telemetry and adjust per workload class.

Risk: Region failover could cause stateful KV-cache churn and client-perceived regressions. Mitigation: coordinate with KV team to expose soft-cache-warm fallback and advertise expected cold-start penalties.
Risk: More SLI data increases metrics cardinality and costs. Mitigation: downsample high-cardinality combos and pre-aggregate in the pipeline by route/variant/region only.
next_steps: Finalize handbook draft and circulate to SRE, Runtime, Console, and Product for sign-off (due 2025-03-05)
Open implementation sub-issues: SLI aggregator (ENG-513580), Circuit state machine (ENG-513581), Console visualization (PM-2745)
Deploy prototype SLI aggregator to staging, run chaos job to simulate 10x burst and validate burn calculation (by 2025-03-10)
Prepare runbook snippets for on-call to interpret graded-SLI alerts and perform controlled regional failover
notes: Prototype uses exponential decay alpha=0.3 for 30s window and alpha=0.1 for 5m window; these are tunable parameters
Soft-degrade actions prioritized: 1) reduce max tokens, 2) switch to quantized model variant, 3) region fallback
We should coordinate with Customer Success to define communication templates for tiered degradation events
